exercise_group.instructions: In Exercises 1–19, mark each statement True or False (T/F). Justify each answer. (If true, cite appropriate facts or theorems. If false, explain why or give a counterexample that shows why the statement is not true in every case.) In Exercises 1–6, $\mathbf{v}_{1},\ldots,\mathbf{v}_{p}$ are vectors in a nonzero finite-dimensional vector space $V$, and $S = \left\{ \mathbf{v}_{1},\ldots,\mathbf{v}_{p} \right\}$.

statement.paragraph: (T/F) The set of all linear combinations of $\mathbf{v}_{1},\ldots,\mathbf{v}_{p}$ is a vector space.
(T/F) If $\left\{ \mathbf{v}_{1}\text{,}\ldots\text{,\,}\mathbf{v}_{p - 1} \right\}$ spans $V$, then $S$ spans $V$.
(T/F) If $\left\{ \mathbf{v}_{1}\text{,}\ldots\text{,\,}\mathbf{v}_{p - 1} \right\}$ is linearly independent, then so is $S$.
(T/F) If $S$ is linearly independent, then $S$ is a basis for $V$.
(T/F) If Span $S = V$, then some subset of $S$ is a basis for $V$.
(T/F) If dim $V = p$ and Span $S = V$, then $S$ cannot be linearly dependent.
(T/F) A plane in $\text{ℝ}^{3}$ is a two-dimensional subspace.
(T/F) The nonpivot columns of a matrix are always linearly dependent.
(T/F) Row operations on a matrix $A$ can change the linear dependence relations among the rows of $A$.
(T/F) Row operations on a matrix can change the null space.
(T/F) The rank of a matrix equals the number of nonzero rows.
(T/F) If an $m \times n$ matrix $A$ is row equivalent to an echelon matrix $U$ and if $U$ has $k$ nonzero rows, then the dimension of the solution space of $A\mathbf{x} = 0$ is $m - k$.
(T/F) If $B$ is obtained from a matrix $A$ by several elementary row operations, then $\text{rank~}B = \text{rank~}A$.
(T/F) The nonzero rows of a matrix $A$ form a basis for Row $A$.
(T/F) If matrices $A$ and $B$ have the same reduced echelon form, then $\text{Row~}A = \text{Row~}B$.
(T/F) If $H$ is a subspace of ${\mathbb{R}}^{3}$, then there is a $3 \times 3$ matrix $A$ such that $H = \text{Col~}A$.
(T/F) If $A$ is $m \times n$ and rank $A = m$, then the linear transformation $\left. \mathbf{x}\mapsto A\mathbf{x} \right.$ is one-to-one.
(T/F) If $A$ is $m \times n$ and the linear transformation $\left. \mathbf{x}\mapsto A\mathbf{x} \right.$ is onto, then rank $A = m$.
(T/F) A change-of-coordinates matrix is always invertible.

Explain what is wrong with the following discussion: Let $\mathbf{f}(t) = 3 + t$ and $\mathbf{g}(t) = 3t + t^{2}$, and note that $\mathbf{g}(t) = t\mathbf{f}(t)$. Then $\{\mathbf{f}\text{,~}\mathbf{g}\}$ is linearly dependent because $\mathbf{g}$ is a multiple of $\mathbf{f}$.

Consider the polynomials $\mathbf{p}_{1}(t) = 1 + t$, $\mathbf{p}_{2}(t) = 1 - t$, $\mathbf{p}_{3}(t) = 4$, $\mathbf{p}_{4}(t) = t + t^{2}$, and $\mathbf{p}_{5}(t) = 1 + 2t + t^{2}$, and let $H$ be the subspace of $\text{ℙ}_{5}$ spanned by the set $S = \{\mathbf{p}_{1}\text{,~}\mathbf{p}_{2}\text{,~}\mathbf{p}_{3}\text{,~}\mathbf{p}_{4}\text{,~}\mathbf{p}_{5}\}$. Use the method described in the proof of the Spanning Set Theorem (Section 4.3) to produce a basis for $H$. (Explain how to select appropriate members of $S$.)

Suppose $\mathbf{p}_{1}$, $\mathbf{p}_{2}$, $\mathbf{p}_{3}$, and $\mathbf{p}_{4}$ are specific polynomials that span a two-dimensional subspace $H$ of $\text{ℙ}_{5}$. Describe how one can find a basis for $H$ by examining the four polynomials and making almost no computations.

What would you have to know about the solution set of a homogeneous system of $18$ linear equations in $20$ variables in order to know that every associated nonhomogeneous equation has a solution? Discuss.
Let $H$ be an $\textit{n}\text{-dimensional}$ subspace of an $\textit{n}\text{-dimensional}$ vector space $V$. Explain why $H = V$.
Let $\left. T:\text{ℝ}^{n}\rightarrow\text{ℝ}^{m} \right.$ be a linear transformation.

list.item: What is the dimension of the range of T if T is a one-to-one mapping? Explain.
What is the dimension of the kernel of T (see Section 4.2) if T maps ℝn onto ℝm? Explain.

statement.paragraph: Let $S$ be a maximal linearly independent subset of a vector space $V$. That is, $S$ has the property that if a vector not in $S$ is adjoined to $S$, then the new set will no longer be linearly independent. Prove that $S$ must be a basis for $V$. [Hint:What if $S$ were linearly independent but not a basis of $V$?]

Let $S$ be a finite minimal spanning set of a vector space $V$. That is, $S$ has the property that if a vector is removed from $S$, then the new set will no longer span $V$. Prove that $S$ must be a basis for $V$.

exercise_group.instructions: Exercises 30–35 develop properties of rank that are sometimes needed in applications. Assume the matrix $A$ is $m \times n$.

statement.paragraph: Show from parts (a) and (b) that rank $AB$ cannot exceed the rank of $A$ or the rank of $B$. (In general, the rank of a product of matrices cannot exceed the rank of any factor in the product.)

list.item: Show that if B is n×p, then rank AB≤rank A. [Hint: Explain why every vector in the column space of AB is in the column space of A.]
Show that if B is n×p, then rank AB≤rank B. [Hint: Use part (a) to study rank (AB)T.]

statement.paragraph: Show that if $P$ is an invertible $m \times m$ matrix, then $\text{rank~}PA = \text{rank~}A$. [Hint:Apply Exercise 30 to $PA$ and $P^{- 1}(PA)$.]
Show that if $Q$ is invertible, then $\text{rank~}AQ = \text{rank~}A$. [Hint:Use Exercise 31 to study $\text{rank~}(AQ)^{T}$.]

Let $A$ be an $m \times n$ matrix, and let $B$ be an $n \times p$ matrix such that ${AB} = 0$. Show that $\text{rank~}A + \text{rank~}B \leq n$. [Hint:One of the four subspaces Nul $A$, Col $A$, Nul $B$, and Col $B$ is contained in one of the other three subspaces.]

If $A$ is an $m \times n$ matrix of rank $r$, then a rank factorization of $A$ is an equation of the form $A = CR$, where $C$ is an $m \times r$ matrix of rank $r$ and $R$ is an $r \times n$ matrix of rank $r$. Show that such a factorization always exists. Then show that given any two $m \times n$ matrices $A$ and $B$.
[Hint: Write $A + B$ as the product of two partitioned matrices.]

A submatrix of a matrix $A$ is any matrix that results from deleting some (or no) rows and/or columns of $A$. It can be shown that $A$ has rank $r$ if and only if $A$ contains an invertible $r \times r$ submatrix and no larger square submatrix is invertible. Demonstrate part of this statement by explaining (a) why an $m \times n$ matrix $A$ of rank $r$ has an $m \times r$ submatrix $A_{1}$ of rank $r$, and (b) why $A_{1}$ has an invertible $r \times r$ submatrix $A_{2}$.
